title: Fixed-object simplicial cofibrations are mappingwise monic
statement: Use small simplicial sets and degreewise injective maps as in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], and the fixed-object model structure on simplicial categories from [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting]. Fix a small set $O$. A simplicial category on $O$ has mapping simplicial sets $A(x,y)$, associative unital simplicial composition and identity vertices; functors fix $O$. A degreewise free extension $A\to B$ means that for each simplicial degree $n$, the ordinary category $B_n$ on $O$ is obtained from $A_n$ by freely adjoining a set of arrows with specified endpoints, without further relations beyond those already in $A_n$ and the category axioms. Every degreewise free extension is injective on $A(x,y)_n\to B(x,y)_n$ for every $x,y\in O$ and every $n\geq0$. The same holds for an arrow retract of such an extension (a retract in the category of identity-on-$O$ simplicial functors and commutative squares). Consequently every cofibration in the fixed-object model structure, whose cofibrations are such retracts as stated in [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting], is a monomorphism on each mapping simplicial set. No Kan or nonemptiness hypothesis on the original mapping sets is imposed.

proof.text: Fix a degree $n$ and put $C=A_n$. Define an auxiliary ordinary category $C^0$ on the same set $O$ by $C^0(x,y)=C(x,y)\amalg\{0_{xy}\}$, using a disjoint new element for every pair. Compose two old arrows by their composition in $C$, and declare any composite involving a new zero arrow to be the new zero arrow with the resulting endpoints. The old identities remain identities: multiplication by an identity fixes old arrows by the laws in $C$ and fixes a new zero by the absorbing rule. Associativity holds because a triple containing a new zero has new-zero composite under both parenthesizations, while a triple of old arrows uses associativity in $C$. The identity-on-$O$ functor $j:C\to C^0$ including the old arrows is injective on every hom set by disjointness.

proof.text: Let $A\to B$ be a degreewise free extension as defined in the statement. For the fixed degree $n$, take the functor $j:A_n\to A_n^0$ of step 1 and assign every freely adjoined generator $x\to y$ the arrow $0_{xy}$. The defining universal property of freely adjoining these arrows extends this assignment to an identity-on-$O$ functor $h:B_n\to A_n^0$ whose restriction to $A_n$ is $j$: the only relations to respect are the old category relations, already respected by $j$, and the category axioms, which hold in $A_n^0$. If two arrows of $A_n(x,y)$ have the same image in $B_n(x,y)$, applying $h$ makes their images under $j$ equal, so they were equal by step 1. This proves injectivity for all $x,y,n$. The auxiliary categories and functors need not be compatible with faces and degeneracies, since the argument is degreewise. To get categorical monicity of each mapping simplicial map, cancel these injective functions in every degree in an equality of two simplicial maps after composition; the original maps then agree in every degree.

source.place: Paragraph 2, coherent coefficient adjunction; agent-written ordinary prerequisite extracted from original lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus proof Step 17. proof.text: Consider any arrow retract $f:A\to C$ of a degreewise free extension $i:D\to B$; the domains need not coincide. Unpacking an arrow retract gives identity-on-$O$ functors $u:A\to D$, $v:C\to B$, $p:D\to A$, $q:B\to C$, satisfying $i\circ u=v\circ f$, $f\circ p=q\circ i$, $p\circ u=\mathrm{id}_A$, and $q\circ v=\mathrm{id}_C$. For $a,a^{\prime}\in A(x,y)_n$ with $f_n(a)=f_n(a^{\prime})$, the square gives $i_n(u_n(a))=v_n(f_n(a))=v_n(f_n(a^{\prime}))=i_n(u_n(a^{\prime}))$. Step 2 implies $u_n(a)=u_n(a^{\prime})$; applying $p_n$ gives $a=a^{\prime}$. All functors fix $O$, so every expression lies in the mapping set for the chosen pair $(x,y)$. This proves degreewise injectivity for arbitrary arrow retracts, and the cancellation argument in step 2 again proves mappingwise monicity.

proof.text: For the fixed-object model structure in the statement, the cited fixed-object simplicial-category result says that every cofibration is an arrow retract of a free simplicial extension. Such an extension is degreewise free as required in step 2; its extra condition that degeneracies preserve the chosen generators is not needed for injectivity. Step 3 therefore applies to every cofibration. The proof used only smallness, the fixed object set, the free-adjunction presentation, and the retract identities. It imposed no Kan or nonemptiness condition on the original mapping simplicial sets.

lean.statement: theorem simplicial_fixed_object_monic_cofibration (O : Type u) : (∀ (A B : Fixed O) (f : A ⟶ B), IsDegreewiseFreeExtension f → (∀ (a b : O) (n : ℕ), Function.Injective ((f.map a b).app (Opposite.op ⦋n⦌))) ∧ (∀ a b : O, Mono (f.map a b))) ∧ (∀ (A B : Fixed O) (f : A ⟶ B), (MorphismProperty.retracts (fun _ _ g ↦ IsDegreewiseFreeExtension (O := O) g)) f → (∀ (a b : O) (n : ℕ), Function.Injective ((f.map a b).app (Opposite.op ⦋n⦌))) ∧ (∀ a b : O, Mono (f.map a b))) ∧ (∀ (A B : Fixed O) (f : A ⟶ B), fixedCofibrations O f → (∀ (a b : O) (n : ℕ), Function.Injective ((f.map a b).app (Opposite.op ⦋n⦌))) ∧ (∀ a b : O, Mono (f.map a b)))
lean.note: The inline degreewise free-extension notion uses the dependency DegreeFunctor and its free-adjunction universal property, without assuming injectivity or degeneracy stability. The three clauses retain degreewise injectivity and mappingwise monicity for free extensions, general arrow retracts and fixed-object cofibrations.
